discoveries.name: Liliuokalani Fourteenth Era: Kahiko / Kahikoluamea, Kupulauakehau, Kulaniehu, Koiaakalani, Hina variants; preceding husband/wife table
discoveries.issue: All preceding spouse pairs are authored as explicitly seeded textual branches, without invented parentage between rows. Wakea’s named parents and Hinakaweoa are authored. Kulaniehu, Koiaakalani and the other Hina forms still need identity decisions.

discoveries.name: Liliuokalani Fifteenth Era: Ole, Pupue, Kamahele, Manaku, Hikohoale, Kahiko, Kaea, Luakahakona, Koulamaikalani, Luanuu, Kawaomaaukele, Kii, Hinakoula, Ulu, Nanaulu, Punuu, Nana, Kapulani, Nanaie, Kahaumokuleia, Nanaielani, Hinakinau, Waikalani, Kekauilani, Kuheleimoana, Mapuuaiaaala, Konohiki, Hakaululena, Waolena, Mahuie, Akalana, Hinaakeahi, four Maui, Kialoa, Kiaakapoko, Pimoe, Mahanauluehu, Hinakeka, Peapea, Moemoe
discoveries.issue: All listed spouses, Ole, Nanaulu, Akalana/Hinaakeahi, the four Maui and named narrative figures are authored. Textual spouse-pair branches enter the audit as explicit seeds; no connecting parent edges were inferred from their order. Comparison with Fornander’s explicit child columns is separately recorded below.

discoveries.name: Fornander island genealogy: Kuluwaiea, Hinanuiakalana/Hinanuialana, Kaulawahine, Hina, Lua, Walinuu, Keaukanai, Uluhina; personified island births
discoveries.source: Fornander first series (1916), Formation and Origin, chs. I–IV
discoveries.issue: Named partners and twelve personified islands are authored with competing cited accounts. Molokini’s afterbirth origin is represented without inventing human parentage. The tentative Haumea/Kuluwaiea interpretation is qualified.

discoveries.name: Piki, Havea Lolofonua, Maui Loa, Maui Puku; named Tangaloa; Takataka and Lomu genealogies
discoveries.issue: Separate records, group records and selectable competing parentages authored. Maatu, Takataka, Collocott as reported by Gifford, and Lomu are not combined.

discoveries.name: Te-more-tu; Te Anu-matao and four fish-class children; Māori Tinirau; Tui Tokelau
discoveries.issue: Named parent and descendant records and source-specific accounts authored; Tokelauan counterpart added. Six of nine Rua daughters are unnamed in this entry; Rua-te-pupuke, Rua-te-hihiko, Rua-te-mahara still require source-specific identity review.

discoveries.name: Sinaleana, Sina of Manu’a, unnamed king of Manu’a; Ariari; Tubo; Vaka-akau-uli
discoveries.issue: Named Samoan branch implemented from Turner XXI. Ariari and cosmical Fe’e implemented from Turner I §§6,8; Tapuaau from IV §8. Tubo and Vaka-akau-uli belong to a separately qualified Tongan Tagaloa context from Tregear. Unnamed partners remain unnamed.

discoveries.name: Tuanui-ka-rere and Tangiia-ka-rere (Mangaian eclipse figures)
discoveries.issue: Corrected the earlier working-note attribution to Atiu. Gill explicitly contrasts Mangaian demons with Rarotongan Tangaroa. Distinct records carry functional comparison, without equating Tuamotuan or other Tangiia figures.

discoveries.name: Disputed Fornander/Lawson cosmogony; Tanaoa, Mutuhei, Atea, Ono, Atanua
discoveries.issue: Descriptions and lifecycle claims now explicitly carry Handy’s authenticity objection. No genealogy or identity is silently deleted.

discoveries.name: Fe’e local cult forms; unnamed Savaii spouse and Upolu chief; Fale
discoveries.issue: The spouse and her father are not personally named. Fale appears as the first-person speaker in the quoted priestly prayer, without enough information to establish a separate biographical record. Local cult contexts are not assigned the cosmical cuttlefish’s parents.

discoveries.name: Fornander’s explicit ancestral tables: Hoohokukalani; Kamole; Hai/Kai; Ulukou; Nanamea; Kapunui/Kapunuu; Hinakawea; Mauiakalana; Hinakealohaila; descendants through Kamehameha; earlier ancestors of Kahiko and Papa
discoveries.source: Fornander first series (1916), Formation/Origin ch. VI and History of Kualii ch. IV
discoveries.issue: Child columns reveal additional direct parentage and variant spellings for many Kumulipo pairs. Partial table read; complete row-by-row identity and family authoring remains, without runtime fuzzy matching. Exact recovered tables and all their named rows are preserved in source-tables.json.

discoveries.name: Kaulu, Kaeha, Makalii and Maoleha nets; Haumea’s death at Niuhelewai
discoveries.source: Fornander first series (1916), Story of Kaulu
discoveries.issue: Primary narrative recovered and death passage read; family, objects and lifecycle claims still to author.

sourceBlockers.impact: The original bibliography was corrected. Gifford supplies attributed variants, so those claims are implemented; direct comparison with the complete Collocott text remains outstanding, not a blocker for Gifford-attributed claims.
